# Output schema of `tdr_static` (reference; pinned by `test_runner_cli`)

`tdr.static.results/2` (this revision adds `tool`, `units`, the per-dataset `nodes` table; the first M8 draft was `/1`). The exact key sets and key order below are asserted by `test_runner_cli` ("the documented schema is exactly what is written"), so this page and the writer cannot drift apart silently.

## 1. Reproducing an experiment
Everything needed is in the result directory: `config.resolved.cfg` is a complete configuration (all 48 keys; seed, instance, vehicle, FLP, neighbourhood, F1/F2, VNS, shake, N4, protocol) and `results.json.tool` names the program version. Re-run `tdr_static run --config <dir>/config.resolved.cfg --out <new dir>`: `results.json`, `runs.csv`, `traces.csv`, `config.resolved.cfg` come out byte-identical (same machine, and across Linux g++ / Windows clang builds in the one case checked, `windows_validation.md`). `manifest.json` lists the FNV-1a 64 digest of each deterministic file (FNV-1a: offset 14695981039346656037, prime 1099511628211, bytes in file order; digest printed as 16 lowercase hex digits; test vectors in `test_runner_cli`), `config_digest` in `results.json` is the same digest of `config.resolved.cfg`. Randomness: one base seed (`seed.base_seed`); instance of dataset d: `derive_seed(base, Instance, d)`; VNS run r: streams `derive_seed(base, Vns, r)` and `derive_seed(base, Shake, r)`; the heuristic TSP seed is the separate key `initial.tsp_heuristic_seed`. Bitwise equality across compilers/libm is not guaranteed in general (the objective is a floating-point sum; the one cross-platform comparison made was identical).

## 2. Conventions
Times and objectives in **seconds** (`*_s`; `*_min` = the same value / 60); coordinates in **metres**; the objective is the **sum over all customers of the service arrival time** (the paper's objective as implemented by `timing_engine`), lower is better. Node ids: depot 0; customers 1..n; flexible launch points (FLPs) n+1 and up (the eager pool of the instance). Numbers are `%.17g` (round-trip exact); non-finite numbers would be `null`. `improvement_pct = 100 (initial - best) / initial` (positive = better than the initial solution). Drone ids are 0-based physical drones.

## 3. `results.json`
Top level: `schema`, `tool`, `units{time, coordinates, objective}`, `experiment`, `datasets[]`.

`experiment`: `name`; `runs_per_dataset`; `num_datasets`; `first_dataset_index`; `first_run_index`; `base_seed`; `config_digest`; `deterministic` (false iff `vns.max_seconds > 0`); `ok` (false: some error occurred); `errors[]` (strings).

`datasets[i]`: `dataset_index`; `instance_seed` (the derived seed actually used); `num_customers`; `num_flp_candidates` (pool size); `initial`; `nodes[]`; `runs[]`; `summary`.
* `initial`: `feasible`; `objective_s/_min`; `num_trips`; `diagnostics[]` (builder / preflight messages); `solution` (absent only with `output.write_solutions=false`).
* `solution`: `truck_route[]` -- node ids in visiting order, depot at both ends, FLP ids appear where a drone is launched from the route; `drone_trips[]` -- `drone`, `launch` (an FLP id), `customer` (served by the drone), `recovery` (customer id or the end depot 0). A trip is flown from `launch` to `customer` and back to the truck at `recovery`, which comes strictly later on the route than `launch`.
* `nodes[]`: `{id, type, x_m, y_m}` with `type` = `depot` | `customer` | `flp`; FLPs add `arc_from`, `arc_to` (the truck arc the FLP lies on) and `position_ratio` (0 = at `arc_from`, 1 = at `arc_to`). The table holds the depot, every customer and every FLP used by the initial solution or any returned solution, so a result can be plotted or re-evaluated without regenerating the instance.
* `summary` (over runs with status ok): `runs_ok`; `best_objective_*`; `best_run_index`; `mean_best_objective_*`; `worst_best_objective_*` (the worst run's best); `std_best_objective_s` (sample standard deviation, n - 1; 0 for one run); `mean_improvement_pct`.

`runs[j]`: `run_index`; `status` (`ok` | `invalid-options` | `initial-infeasible`); `stop` (`iter-max` | `no-improvement` | `time-limit` | `none`); `verified` (the runner re-checked the best solution: every customer once, evaluator-feasible, exact objective); `initial_objective_*`, `best_objective_*`, `final_current_objective_*` (the accepted solution at the end; `best` is the best-so-far); `improvement_pct`; `iterations` (passes performed); `t0`, `final_temperature`; `best_updates`, `last_best_iteration`; `improving_moves`, `sa_accepted_moves`; `passes{completed, skipped, guard_truncated, guard_triggered, local_steps_total, max_local_steps_in_pass}` (`completed + skipped + guard_truncated = iterations`; `guard_triggered` = the `max_local_steps` guard cut at least one pass's local search); `shakes{applied, not_applicable_redraws, infeasible_redraws, applied_by_kind{reverse, exchange, shift, drone_remove}}`; `operators[8]` for N1..N8: `calls`, `no_anchor` (operator not applicable), `no_candidate` (applicable, no feasible candidate), `improving`, `sa_accepted`, `sa_rejected`; `num_trips` and `best_solution` (as `solution`).

## 4. Other files
* `runs.csv`: header `dataset_index,run_index,status,stop,verified,initial_objective_s,best_objective_s,best_objective_min,improvement_pct,iterations,passes_completed,passes_skipped,passes_guard_truncated,guard_triggered,shakes_applied,shakes_not_applicable,shakes_infeasible,improving_moves,sa_accepted_moves,best_updates,last_best_iteration,t0,final_temperature,num_trips`; one row per run; same values as `results.json`.
* `traces.csv` (only with `output.record_trace`): `dataset_index,run_index,iter,temperature,shaken,shake_kind,pass_end,local_steps,moves,current_objective_s,best_objective_s`; `shake_kind`: -1 none, 0 reverse, 1 exchange, 2 shift, 3 drone_remove; `pass_end`: `completed` | `skipped` | `guard-truncated`; `temperature` is the T used in that pass; `current` / `best` are the objectives at the end of the pass.
* `timing.json` (`tdr.static.timing/1`): `schema`, `note`, `total_seconds`, `runs[]{dataset_index, run_index, seconds}` -- wall clock, the only non-deterministic content.
* `manifest.json` (`tdr.static.manifest/1`): `schema`, `tool`, `experiment`, `deterministic`, `ok`, `files[]{name, bytes, fnv1a64}` (`not-reproducible` for `timing.json`).
* `config.resolved.cfg`: `key = value` lines, see `tdr_static list-keys`.

## 5. Sufficiency check (what is and is not in the files)
Sufficient to: rerun the experiment exactly; verify digests; interpret every objective and counter; plot the instance and any written solution (node table); compare runs, datasets and settings statistically (all run-level numbers in `runs.csv`). Not recorded: compiler and library versions (the byte-identity claim is empirical), the git revision of the code (the repository is uncommitted; `tool` carries the program version string only), and per-candidate operator diagnostics (only per-operator call and acceptance counts).
